title: The Lantern
logline: A neighbourhood spends weeks building a great Vesak lantern of bamboo and paper, lights it for a few nights, then takes it apart.
human_question: Why do we pour so much into something we know will be taken apart, and what is it while it lasts?

premise.story: A community lantern (thorana or kuduwa) from bamboo frame to dismantling.
premise.experience: Bamboo, glue, paper, light, crowds, and then the bare frame.

concept_links.why: Aggregates and the truths: a named whole assembled, seen, and dissolved. The reason for seeing clearly is suffering and its end.
A collective and shape concept that exists only while its parts are arranged.

what_must_be_real: The actual builders, budget, disagreements and timeline.

possible_arc.ending_open: Taken apart. What the builders feel then leads directly into wanting (Group 2).

position_hint: closing candidate: hands off from wonder to wanting

requirements: A lantern or thorana build during Vesak
Access across build, lighting and dismantling

suggestions.name: A Colombo neighbourhood known for Vesak thoranas
suggestions.verify: Access, permissions and current conditions are unverified.

suggestions.name: A small-town Vesak lantern competition
suggestions.verify: Access, permissions and current conditions are unverified.

risks: Festival spectacle without a person to follow
drop_if: Only spectacle footage; no builders who will share the process

connections.note: A whole assembled from parts and dissolved again.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
